item.title: Idioms at work
item.description: Common idioms for meetings, projects and office life.

children.definition: to start an activity or process
children.example: Let's get the ball rolling with a quick update from each team.

children.definition: agreeing about what to do, or understanding something in the same way
children.example: Before we email the client, let's make sure we're all on the same page.

children.definition: to do something badly or cheaply in order to save time or money
children.example: If we cut corners on testing, the app will crash later.

children.definition: used when a plan has failed and you must start planning again
children.example: The client rejected the design, so it's back to the drawing board.

children.definition: a number that is a rough estimate, not an exact amount
children.example: Can you give me a ballpark figure for the cost?

children.definition: to contact someone briefly to share news or check progress
children.example: I'll touch base with you on Friday about the schedule.

children.definition: to do your fair share of the work
children.example: Everyone on the team needs to pull their weight if we want to finish on time.

children.definition: to stop working for the rest of the day
children.example: It's nearly eight o'clock. Let's call it a day.
Our plans for the new office are still up in the air.

children.definition: the process of learning something new and difficult, and how quickly it happens
children.example: The new accounting software has a steep learning curve.

children.definition: the most important fact in a situation
children.example: The bottom line is that we can't finish by Monday.
Please keep me in the loop about any changes to the contract.
